details:
When on the dancefloor of Tube and Shelter VR Clubs, I'm unable to take photographs without crashing when the space is crowded. This first happened to me July 30th and has been a huge issue to me since then, as photos are a big part of what I do in VRChat. This month I've been to many crowded events (VREgypt, Contact)   with full 80/40 instances, but never had issues. That said this is not a random issue, I've spent 10+ hours during the nights of these events troubleshooting and trying to isolate the problem, so I'll share my findings: 
Crashing can be caused by the following:
- Taking VR photos (VRClens or otherwise)
- Having stream camera open / opening it
- Taking countdown desktop mode photos (beta)
Often the crashing occurred immediately after taking a photo, or sometimes I could get a few photos in before conditions worsened and taking a photo caused crashing. If I used the beta to hide non-friend characters, I was able to use the camera comfortably. It's clear the issue only happens under stress, but like I mentioned, i'm usually able to take photos of full crowds when i'm at 9-12FPS, and during these instances where I crashed, I was usually at 19-20fps.
If I had to say what aspects of TUBE and Shelter are similar, it would be that they both use shaders to change the look of avatars, however TUBE has a button to disable this, and the issue remained. They also both stretch their streams out over the room, and use VRCDN bots for instance control. I can take photos anywhere else on the map, just not the crowded dancefloor. 
Hardware:
GPU: NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1080 Ti
CPU: Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-9400F CPU @ 2.90GHz (6 CPUs)
RAM: 16GB on one stick
Here is a list of the things I've tried to solve this issue without success: 
• Change avatar
• Enable beta, disable beta
• Change photo size
• Remove peripherals (keyboard, audio, other HDDs)
• Switch from my NVME to SSD Drive (fresh windows install) 
• Use PC mode which honestly crashed even more. I was able to use F12 to take screen shots for a while, but then I crashed from just being there in PC mode. 
Other notes: 
• Sometimes the photo that crashed me will be saved, but usually it isn't there 
• Photos are saved to C:\Users\[user]\Pictures , but there is a vrchat album present in my onedrive folder, however I don't use onedrive
• All of my photos recently have been rotated wrong occasionally, like one in a series will be 90 degreees left of where it should be, even though there was no change in the camera orientation
title: Crashing when using camera in specific crowded spaces
